title: Who should hold the Twister
notes: PWYF's Midi Fighter Twister serves the pedals, scenes and the looper. This says who SHOULD hold it now; Helm's hub says who does (its claim on the Twister's output is the record, and nobody paints a Twister they do not hold). Plan docs/kb/plans/quadrat-the-sampler.md, phase 3.

The table (AC, 2026-11-05; itajara/controllers Data.Looper.TwisterHolder): an MC6 bank can name who holds the Twister, and when it does, that holder has it. A scene's bank names PWYF (bank-scene); the looper's bank names the looper's own process (bank-looper); any other bank names nobody (bank-plain), and the focused pedal has it. While a bank names a holder, focus changes are remembered by the host and change nothing on the device.
Leaving a bank that named a holder hands the Twister back to the pedal page (the focused pedal's knobs, or dark rings if none is focused).

Every arrival is an entry, and entries act: paint-pedal and paint-scene paint if PWYF holds the Twister and ask the hub for it if not (painting when granted); hand-to-looper grants it to the looper's process if PWYF holds it. Focusing what is already focused re-enters on purpose, because PWYF has always repainted then.

2026-11-07: the looper stopped being a pedal in PWYF (AC: "remove the pill and that control page"), so it can no longer be focused. Removed: the state looper (the looper's pages by focus), the event focus-looper, and the fact pedal-focused, which only chose between a focused pedal and the looper on leaving a holder's bank. The MC6 standing on the looper's bank is now the only way the Twister reaches the looper.

Transcribed from Component.App 2026-11-04, not designed; reshaped 2026-11-05 when the looper's pages moved to the looper's own process. Before this machine, a frame from the daemon or a side button could paint over a scene.
